summary: All three tasks are correctly implemented and well-tested. The security fix properly addresses the plaintext gRPC channel vulnerability by honoring the `functions-uri` scheme: `https` URIs now use TLS transport security, `http` and legacy host+port continue using plaintext, and unsupported schemes fail fast. Backward compatibility is maintained through a Java 8 default interface method on `IApplication`. Test coverage includes unit tests for transport selection logic, Application argument precedence, and integration tests verifying plaintext connectivity, TLS connectivity, and no-downgrade behavior. All three workers report successful `mvn test` runs with 73 total tests passing.

findings.description: The @Nullable annotation on useTransportSecurity() relies on a transitive dependency from grpc-api (jsr305) rather than an explicit POM dependency. This works but could break if the grpc dependency tree changes. Low risk since grpc-api has had this transitive dependency for years.

The FunctionsTestHost handleMessage() was refactored from indefinite await() to timeout-based waiting with throwIfListeningFailed() checks. While this is an improvement, it changes existing test infrastructure behavior beyond the strict scope of TLS support. The change is safe but worth noting.
